title: Seeing Bill Bojangles Robinson dance in wooden shoes
summary: He recalls seeing Bojangles Robinson at a medicine show and Willard asks how the wooden-soled dancing shoes worked.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: But years later when we were traveling on the carnivals, they had some great, great dancers -- and I remember, I saw Bill Bojangles Robinson with a Medicine Show. I don't know if you're familiar with what Medicine Shows were. Medicine Shows were things that just went around from town to town with a wagon, and they would open up there and they'd have some kind of little stage built there. Well, they had -- dancers used to dance in wooden shoes at the time, that I'm speaking of. You know, this was ... I must have been 6 or 7 years old.
Were they a special dancing shoe? Not like a Dutch wooden shoe?
No. No. They were really dancing shoes, and instead of having taps on the heels and the toes, well, the shoe in its entirety was a wooden shoe.

No. No. It would be leather, and just the soul would be wood. And they used to -- I don't really know, but I would imagine that's what they were talking about with some dance they called the 'Clog'? I don't know whether you ever heard of that, you know, but they did that with wooden shoes.
